units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay. A bridge again.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A different one. This is the LaSalle Street Bridge.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It opened on December 20, 1928, and it carries LaSalle Street over the main stem of the river.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It connects the Loop with the Near North Side.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Was it new, then, like the Michigan Avenue one?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Close. Widening LaSalle Street and improving the Loop's access to the north side was proposed as early as 1902, and the design was approved in 1916.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The designer was Donald Becker, and a company called Strobel Steel built it, for two and a half million dollars.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Two and a half million dollars.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's a single-deck, double-leaf bascule bridge.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: That means two halves of the roadway lift upward so boats can pass.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The same idea as the one you crossed yesterday, but only one deck.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And does it have a name?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It does. In 1999 the Chicago City Council renamed it the Marshall Suloway Bridge, after a former commissioner of the Department of Public Works.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Does anyone call it that?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Mostly, people still say LaSalle Street Bridge.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Naturally.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Cross to the north bank. The steakhouse is right there, in a glass-walled dining room on the river.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Pause, enjoy dinner, and then come back.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And the walk back?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Same bridge, same river, but look at it differently.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: You'll be walking east along Wacker Drive to the hotel's Wacker entrance, about twelve minutes.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And Bar Pendry is right inside, with its fireplace.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: A fireplace. Finally, a promise.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And you don't have to go outside again afterward.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The elevator goes up to your room.
